title: Mapped field returns empty or undefined value at runtime
problem: A module field is mapped to a variable from a previous module, but at runtime that variable is empty, null, or undefined. If the field is required, the module fails. If optional, the module silently sends an empty value to the external service.
symptoms: Module fails with a required field error on a field that appears mapped
Module silently sends empty or null values to the external service
Downstream records are created with missing data
Error is inconsistent — happens only for some records, not all

likely_causes.cause: The source field is optional in the API response and is absent for some records
The previous module returned 0 results, making all its output variables undefined
The mapped path is incorrect (wrong nesting level or wrong field name)
The field existed during scenario design but the source API changed its response structure

diagnosis_steps: Run the scenario with 'Run once' using a record where the error occurs
Inspect the output bundle of the module that should provide the value
Verify whether the field appears in the bundle or is absent for this specific record
Check whether the field path is correctly mapped — the field may be nested differently in some cases
Compare a failing record against a succeeding record: identify what is structurally different
Check whether any upstream module could return 0 results (search modules, lookup modules) — if so, all downstream variables are undefined

solutions.solution: Wrap optional mapped values with ifempty() to provide a fallback: {{ifempty(1.email; 'default@domain.com')}}
solutions.conditions: When the field is optional and a fallback value is acceptable for the use case

solutions.solution: Add a filter before the failing module checking that the required field exists: use 'Exists' condition on the field
solutions.conditions: When the record should be skipped entirely if the required field is missing

solutions.solution: Use the get() function to safely access nested properties that may not always exist: {{get(1.data; 'user.email')}}
solutions.conditions: When the field is accessed through a deeply nested path that may not exist on all records

solutions.solution: Add a Tools > Set Variables module after the source module to normalize all optional fields with explicit default values before downstream modules
solutions.conditions: When multiple fields need defensive defaults applied in one place

prevention: Treat every optional API field as potentially absent — always add ifempty() guards on optional mappings
Add filters before modules with required fields to validate data completeness upstream
Test scenarios explicitly with edge-case records (missing fields, null values, empty strings)

title: Data type mismatch in module field
problem: Make passes a value of an incorrect type to a module field or external API. The target module or external API rejects the value with a validation or type error.
symptoms: Module fails with a type or validation error
Date fields are rejected despite appearing correctly formatted visually
Number fields fail when the value contains a comma decimal separator
Boolean fields fail when passed as the string 'true' or 'false'

likely_causes.cause: A date returned as an ISO string is not in the exact format required by the target API or module
A number is returned with a locale-specific decimal separator (comma) instead of a period
A boolean value is serialized as the string 'true' or 'false' instead of a native boolean
An array is passed where a single value is expected, or a single value where an array is expected

diagnosis_steps: Open the failing module and inspect the input bundle in the execution details
Identify the type tag shown for the problematic field (Text, Number, Boolean, Date, Array, Collection)
Compare with the type expected by the module's field or the target API documentation
Test the relevant conversion function (formatDate, parseNumber, etc.) in the Make formula editor with a sample value

solutions.solution: Use formatDate() to convert dates to the exact format required by the target: {{formatDate(1.date; 'YYYY-MM-DD')}}
solutions.conditions: When a date is passed in a format not accepted by the target module or API

solutions.solution: Use parseNumber() to convert locale-formatted numbers: {{parseNumber(1.amount; ',')}}
solutions.conditions: When a number uses a comma as decimal separator but the API expects a period

solutions.solution: Use the if() function to convert string booleans to native booleans: {{if(1.active = 'true'; true; false)}}
solutions.conditions: When a boolean is stored as the string 'true' or 'false'

solutions.solution: Use toString() or toNumber() for direct type coercion when the conversion is straightforward
solutions.conditions: For simple type conversions where no formatting transformation is needed

prevention: Inspect bundle value types in the bundle inspector before mapping to modules with strict type requirements
Add a Set Variables module to normalize data types before critical API modules
Test with edge-case values during development (locale-formatted numbers, different date formats)

title: JSON parsing or serialization error
problem: Make fails to parse a JSON string into a structured data object, or an HTTP module receives a response body that is not valid JSON despite being expected to be.
symptoms: HTTP module or Webhook module cannot parse the response body into structured fields
Iterator receives a string instead of an array after a parseJSON() call
Data appears as raw text instead of structured fields in the bundle inspector
parseJSON() function throws an error on execution

likely_causes.cause: The API response body is not valid JSON — it may be an HTML error page, truncated content, or have encoding issues
The Webhook body type setting does not match the actual incoming payload format (Raw vs JSON vs Form Data)
The JSON string contains syntax errors such as unescaped special characters or trailing commas
The Content-Type header of the response does not declare the actual body format

diagnosis_steps: Open the failing execution and inspect the raw response body received by the module
Paste the body into a JSON validator to identify the exact syntax error location
Check the Content-Type header of the response — it should be application/json for JSON bodies
Verify that the Webhook body type setting matches the actual incoming payload format
Check whether the response is an HTML error page returned instead of JSON (common when APIs return errors in HTML)

solutions.solution: Verify that the HTTP module has the correct 'Parse response' configuration so Make interprets the body as JSON and creates structured bundle fields
solutions.conditions: When the body is valid JSON but Make is treating it as raw text

solutions.solution: Switch the Webhook body type setting (Raw / JSON / Form Data) to match the actual incoming payload format
solutions.conditions: When a webhook receives correct data but the body type setting is misconfigured

solutions.solution: Add an Error Handler on the HTTP module to catch JSON parse failures and route to an alert notification
solutions.conditions: When the source API occasionally returns invalid JSON and graceful failure handling is needed

prevention: Validate sample JSON responses from the API in a JSON linter during scenario development
Set the correct body type on webhook triggers before expecting structured field access
Add Error Handlers on HTTP modules that parse external API responses

title: Collection mapped where Array is expected — or Array mapped where Collection is expected
problem: Make distinguishes between Arrays (ordered lists of items, iterable) and Collections (key-value objects, not directly iterable). Mapping a Collection where an Array is expected — or vice versa — causes downstream modules to fail or produce incorrect output.
symptoms: Iterator fails or produces a single unexpected bundle instead of multiple item bundles
Module expecting a list field receives an object and fails
Bundle inspector shows type 'Collection' where type 'Array' was expected
Aggregator output is a single merged object instead of a list

likely_causes.cause: An API response wraps an array inside a parent object (e.g., {items: [...]}) and the mapping targets the parent object instead of the nested array
The module produces a Collection (object) but downstream expects an Array — a conversion step is missing

diagnosis_steps: Open the execution and inspect the bundle type in the bundle inspector — look for the type label (Array vs Collection)
If the bundle shows 'Collection' where 'Array' is expected, identify the parent object path and map to the specific nested array field
If the bundle shows 'Array' where 'Collection' is expected, check whether the module is correctly configured to return a single object

solutions.solution: Map the downstream module or Iterator to the specific nested array field, not the parent wrapper object. For example, map to 1.data.items instead of 1.data.
solutions.conditions: When an API response wraps the array inside a parent object

solutions.solution: Use the Array Aggregator to convert an iterated set of Collections into a single Array when a module downstream requires an Array input
solutions.conditions: When individual Collection bundles need to be assembled into an Array

prevention: Always inspect the type tag (Array vs Collection) in the bundle inspector before connecting an Iterator or any module requiring a specific type
When mapping nested data, navigate through the bundle hierarchy in the mapping panel rather than guessing the path

origin_details.evidence: Make distinguishes Array and Collection as separate data types with different behaviors. Array is iterable by Iterator; Collection is a key-value structure.

evidence.claim: Make's data types include Array (ordered, iterable) and Collection (key-value, not directly iterable) as distinct types

sequence: source returns object with nested array
Iterator or downstream receives Collection not Array
conditions: API response wraps array in a parent object
Mapping targets wrapper instead of nested array

diagnostic_signals: Bundle inspector shows type 'Collection' on a field expected to be 'Array'
Iterator produces 1 bundle (the whole object) instead of N bundles (the items)
[observed message variant] "Unable to iterate over non-array value"
audit_notes: Array vs Collection distinction confirmed in Make data types documentation. The nesting issue (API wrapping arrays in objects) is a very common real-world pattern confirmed in community.

title: Null value propagates silently through mapping chain
problem: A null or undefined value enters a mapping chain and propagates through multiple downstream modules without triggering an error. Each module silently passes null forward until a module that cannot accept null fails — often far from the original source of the null.
symptoms: A module fails with a required-field error but the mapped field appears correct in the mapping panel
The null originates several modules back — the failing module is not the root cause
Error is data-dependent — occurs for some records but not others
Setting a breakpoint (using Run once) shows intermediate bundles contain null for the affected field

likely_causes.cause: A source field is absent in some API records but present in others — null propagates silently where it is absent
A module that performs a lookup or search returns 0 results — all downstream mappings from that module become null
An ifempty() or default value guard is missing on an optional source field

diagnosis_steps: Use 'Run once' with the failing record and inspect each bundle in the execution, starting from the source module
Trace the null field backward through each module's output bundle until you find where it first becomes null
Check whether the source API response includes the field for this specific record
Check whether an upstream search or lookup module returned 0 results, making all its output fields null

solutions.solution: Add ifempty(mapped_field; fallback_value) at the earliest point in the chain where the field can be null. Do not wait until the failing module to add the guard.
solutions.conditions: When the null originates from an optional source field

solutions.solution: Add a filter after the search or lookup module to stop processing when 0 results are returned, before the null values reach downstream modules
solutions.conditions: When the null originates from a module returning 0 results

solutions.solution: Add a Set Variables module immediately after the source module to normalize all potentially-null fields with explicit defaults
solutions.conditions: When multiple fields can be null and each needs a different default

prevention: Add null guards (ifempty or filter) as early as possible in the chain — at the first module that can produce a null value
Always handle the 0-results case for search and lookup modules before proceeding to downstream mapping

origin_details.evidence: ifempty() function is documented for handling null/empty values in mappings.

evidence.claim: Make's ifempty() function handles null and empty values in mappings by providing a fallback
When a module returns 0 results, all mapped output fields from that module are undefined/null in downstream bundles

sequence: source returns record without optional field
action module receives null on required field
conditions: Optional source field absent for this record
No ifempty() guard between source and consumer

diagnostic_signals: Error occurs at a module distant from the source of the null
Same scenario works for some records but not others
Run once shows null in intermediate bundle for the affected field
Upstream search module returned 0 results
audit_notes: ifempty() confirmed in Make documentation. Null propagation behavior is consistent with Make's execution model and widely reported in community. The pattern of tracing null backward through the chain is a diagnostic approach, not an explicitly documented Make procedure.

title: Date format mismatch between source and target module
problem: A date value is correctly present in the source module output but is rejected by the target module or external API because the date format does not match what the target expects. Make date handling requires explicit format conversion using formatDate().
symptoms: A date field causes a 422 or validation error at the target API
The date value appears correct visually in the mapping panel but is rejected
Different modules return dates in different formats — some accepted, some rejected

likely_causes.cause: The source module returns a date in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2026-09-02T10:00:00Z) but the target API expects a different format (e.g., DD/MM/YYYY or Unix timestamp)
The date value is a string, not a Make Date type — the target module requires a native Date type
Time zone offset in the date string is not handled by the target API as expected

diagnosis_steps: Inspect the date value in the source bundle — note the exact format and type (Date vs Text)
Check the target API documentation for the exact date format required
Test the formatDate() conversion in the Make formula editor with the source value before applying it in the scenario

solutions.solution: Use formatDate(source_date; 'YYYY-MM-DD') or the required format string to convert the date before passing it to the target module. Refer to Make's formatDate() documentation for format tokens.
solutions.conditions: When the source and target use different date format strings

solutions.solution: Use parseDate() to convert a date string to a Make Date type first, then formatDate() to output in the target format
solutions.conditions: When the source value is a string that needs to be parsed before formatting

solutions.solution: Use formatDate(source_date; 'X') to convert to Unix timestamp when the target API requires it
solutions.conditions: When the target API expects a Unix timestamp

prevention: Always check the target API's date format requirement before mapping date fields
Use formatDate() explicitly on every date mapping — never assume the source format matches the target

origin_details.source_name: Make Help Center — Date and time functions
origin_details.evidence: formatDate() and parseDate() are documented in Make's date and time functions reference.

evidence.claim: Make provides formatDate() to convert dates to a specified format string
Make provides parseDate() to parse a date string into a Make Date type

modules: HTTP or integration module (strict date format)
sequence: source returns date in format A
conditions: No formatDate() conversion between source and target

diagnostic_signals: 422 validation error on a date field
Date value present in source bundle but rejected by target
Different date-related modules return dates in different formats
audit_notes: formatDate() and parseDate() confirmed in Make documentation. Date format mismatch is a very common and well-documented class of mapping error.

title: Number formatting mismatch — comma vs period decimal separator
problem: A numeric value is returned with a locale-specific decimal separator (comma, e.g. 1,234.56 or 1.234,56) that differs from what the target API or module expects. The target rejects the number or silently truncates it.
symptoms: A number field causes a type or validation error at the target
A numeric value is silently truncated — 1.234,56 becomes 1 after parsing
Calculations produce wrong results because a string is passed where a number is expected

likely_causes.cause: The source system uses a comma as a decimal separator (European locale) but the target API expects a period
The number is returned as a string with a thousands separator that prevents numeric parsing

diagnosis_steps: Inspect the number value in the source bundle — check whether it is typed as Number or Text
Check whether the value contains a comma or period as the decimal separator
Test parseNumber() with the correct separator argument in the formula editor

solutions.solution: Use parseNumber(source_value; ',') to convert a comma-decimal number to a Make Number type. The second argument specifies the decimal separator used in the source string.
solutions.conditions: When the source uses comma as decimal separator

solutions.solution: Use the replace() function to remove thousands separators before parseNumber(): replace(source_value; '.'; '') to remove periods as thousands separators before parsing
solutions.conditions: When the value contains thousands separators that prevent clean parsing

prevention: Always inspect the type and format of numeric fields from external sources before mapping to numeric fields
Apply parseNumber() with the explicit separator argument for any number coming from a non-English locale source

origin_details.evidence: parseNumber() with decimal separator argument is documented in Make's math functions reference.

evidence.claim: Make's parseNumber(value; decimalSeparator) function converts a formatted number string to a numeric type, accepting the decimal separator as an argument

sequence: target rejects or silently parses as 1
conditions: Source uses comma as decimal separator

diagnostic_signals: Numeric field rejected with type or validation error
Numeric value contains comma — may be a decimal or thousands separator
Bundle inspector shows type 'Text' on a field expected to be 'Number'
audit_notes: parseNumber() with separator argument confirmed in Make documentation. European locale numeric format is a common real-world issue.

title: Boolean value passed as string 'true'/'false' instead of native boolean
problem: A boolean field is returned from a source as the string 'true' or 'false' rather than a native boolean type. The target module or API expects a native boolean and rejects the string value.
symptoms: A boolean/checkbox field at the target receives 'true' or 'false' as text and is rejected
Bundle inspector shows type 'Text' on a field that should be boolean
Conditional logic on the field does not work correctly — 'false' (string) evaluates as truthy in some contexts

likely_causes.cause: The source API serializes booleans as JSON strings rather than native boolean values
A previous mapping or text transformation converted a boolean to a string

diagnosis_steps: Inspect the field value type in the bundle inspector — confirm it shows 'Text' instead of 'Boolean'
Check the source API response — is the value 'true'/'false' (string) or true/false (boolean) in the raw JSON?
If it is a string, use the if() function to convert it before passing to the target

solutions.solution: Use the if() function to convert string boolean to native boolean: {{if(1.active = 'true'; true; false)}}
solutions.conditions: When the source returns 'true' or 'false' as a string

prevention: Check the type of boolean fields from external APIs in the bundle inspector before mapping to boolean-type target fields
Apply if() conversion consistently on any boolean field that arrives as a string

origin_details.evidence: Make distinguishes Boolean as a data type separate from Text. The if() function for conversion is documented in general functions.

evidence.claim: Make's Boolean data type is distinct from Text — a string 'true' is not equivalent to a native boolean true
The if() function can be used to convert a string boolean to a native boolean in Make mappings

sequence: mapping passes string to boolean field

diagnostic_signals: Bundle inspector shows type 'Text' on a field that should be Boolean
Conditional logic on a boolean field produces unexpected results
422 validation error on a boolean/checkbox field
audit_notes: Removed an unverified conversion function recommendation. Remaining guidance is conditional and requires verification on the actual input.

title: Variable unavailable because of execution order or lifetime
problem: Get Variable requires Set Variable to have executed earlier and the variable lifetime to cover the read.
symptoms: Get Variable returns an unexpected or missing value.

likely_causes.cause: The setter has not run yet, or its lifetime has ended.

diagnosis_steps: Inspect route order, filters, variable name and lifetime.

solutions.solution: Run the setter before the getter and choose the appropriate cycle or execution lifetime.
solutions.conditions: The read depends on a scenario variable.

prevention: Check setter execution for every path.

origin_details.evidence: Get Variable can read a variable set on another route if Set Variable executed earlier.

evidence.claim: Get Variable can read a variable set on another route if Set Variable executed earlier.

diagnostic_signals: Variable missing at read time
audit_notes: Documentary correction 2026-09-08; no verified real-case resolution.

title: Accessing array items by index — wrong index or out-of-bounds
problem: When accessing a specific item from an array using index notation or the get() function, the wrong index is used (Make arrays are 1-indexed, not 0-indexed) or the index exceeds the array length, returning undefined.
symptoms: An array item is empty or undefined despite the array containing data
The first item of an array returns empty when accessed with index 0
An array access that worked for test data fails for smaller arrays in production

likely_causes.cause: Using index 0 to access the first array item — Make arrays are 1-indexed (first item = index 1)
Accessing an index that exceeds the array length for some records (e.g., always accessing item 3 when some records have fewer items)

diagnosis_steps: Check the index being used — for Make's 1-indexed arrays, the first item is at index 1, not 0
Check the array length in the bundle inspector for the failing record — it may be shorter than expected
Use the length() function to verify array length before accessing by index

solutions.solution: Change index 0 to index 1 to access the first array item: {{1.items[1]}} not {{1.items[0]}}
solutions.conditions: When using index 0 expecting the first item — the most common array indexing mistake

solutions.solution: Use ifempty() with a fallback when the index may not exist: {{ifempty(1.items[3]; 'default')}}
solutions.conditions: When the array length varies and the index may be out of bounds for some records

prevention: Remember Make arrays are 1-indexed — always use index 1 for the first element
When accessing a fixed index, verify that all possible records have at least that many items

origin_details.evidence: Make arrays are 1-indexed. This is a fundamental Make data type behavior.

evidence.claim: Make arrays use 1-based indexing — the first element is at index 1, not 0

conditions: Using 0-based indexing assumption on a 1-indexed Make array

diagnostic_signals: First array item returns empty when accessed with index 0
Array has data but mapped index returns undefined
Worked in test with large arrays but fails with smaller arrays in production
audit_notes: 1-based array indexing is a fundamental Make behavior confirmed in documentation. Common source of confusion for developers coming from 0-indexed languages.
